clue.text: What's popular in jazz develops slowly in commercial areas

clue.text: Bear right in the country

the outside letters of the word

clue.text: Ex-serviceman, ambassador and lawyer in state avert disaster

clue.text: Refuse Roger in bed

clue.text: Starting with this, finish up in endless pain needing treatment?

taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a tingling numbness can be the first sign of nerve trouble that ends in chronic pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins and needles is the prickling sensation in a limb, an early warning symptom before something worse.

clue.text: Names mangled, one beginning to corpse?

definitions.text: Names mangled, one beginning to corpse?

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
the start of the following word supplies just its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Roman numeral for one
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An actor who garbles the cast's names is about to corpse, i.e. dissolve into giggles on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone who mangles names, a person starting to fail on stage, could be suffering memory loss. To corpse is theatre slang for breaking down mid-scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with amnesia forgets, so mangled names and a performer losing lines picture a memory-loss sufferer.

clue.text: Cooking oil used with Indian dish

clue.text: Wading bird, one alongside twice

clue.text: One intact at sea? Not exactly
